published_statement: NOT READ AT SOURCE THIS RUN. As the tree records it (hpscentre.py:245): 'F(l) ~ (a ln l - b)^2, HPS p.8' with a = 5.3, b = 25.5 -- the far-zone behaviour of HPS's numerical throat solution from their eq. (9) data, ln f(0) = -2/3 (hpscentre.py:246). The tree's characterisation (hpscentre.py:169-176): 'a two-parameter log fit ... HPS do not state the window they fitted over.' No verbatim sentence of HPS p.8 could be quoted here.
published_hypotheses: (as recorded by the tree, not re-read) HPS's semiclassical system: Einstein equations sourced by the AHS analytic (DeWitt-Schwinger-type) approximation to <T_ab> for a massless conformally coupled scalar (xi = 1/6), static spherical ansatz ds^2 = -f dt^2 + dl^2 + r(l)^2 dOmega^2 (hpscentre.py:112-128; qeihps.py:55-58 per sibling audit 1208.5399-sec5.1)
(as recorded) boundary data eq. (9): throat at l = 0, r'(0) = f'(0) = 0, ln f(0) = -2/3 for the run fitted, -1 <= ln f(0) < 0 allowed (hpscentre.py:246-247)
(as recorded) lengths in units of K, K^2 = 1/(5760 pi) l_P^2 (hpscentre.py:890-893); b is only meaningful with this unit (see rederivation A1)
(as recorded) the fit is over some far-zone range of l that HPS do not state (hpscentre.py:176, 252)

(implied by the law itself, computed) the law can hold only for l >> l0 = exp(b/a) = 122.9 (HPS unit), and it makes F unbounded (F(1e5) = 1262 by the law), i.e. g_tt does not tend to a constant: consistent with Hochberg-Visser gr-qc/9802046 p.3 'no asymptotically flat spatial regions' and with the tree's quote of HPS 'the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat' (hpscentre.py:99-100)
hypothesis_drift: UNIT OF l (implicit, not flagged in the tree): hpscentre.py:252 takes the windows '(lo, hi, sampling) in K' and matches b = 25.5 in K units (hpscentre.py:923-927). b is NOT unit-invariant: l -> lam l sends b -> b - a ln lam (sympy, A1). Had HPS's l been in l_P, the K-unit target would be b = 51.48, not 25.5. Evidence either way: the tree's printed-M1 integration reproduces (5.3, 25.5) within 5 % IN K UNITS in 125 of 231 windows, which supports (does not prove) the K reading; b = 51.48 is also reached by the conserved run at large windows (max b 57.5), so the reproduction alone does not exclude it. Not re-read at source: named hypothesis, not a finding.

SYMBOL F vs f: hpscentre.py:245's comment writes 'F(l) ~ (a ln l - b)^2' while far_zone_fit (hpscentre.py:911-920) fits sqrt of the state variable y[0] = f (the g_tt redshift function; y0[0] = exp(ln f(0)), hpscentre.py:978). The identification F = f is the tree's reading; unverified this run.

WINDOW ADDED BY THE TREE (a hypothesis HPS's figure lacks, per the tree): hpscentre.py:169-176, 252 'HPS do not state the window'. The tree's use is therefore NARROWER than a bare 'far-zone law': it treats (5.3, 25.5) as window-dependent and uses it only as a fixture (hpscentre.py:241-245 'used ONLY as fixtures to compare against'). This drift is in the conservative direction and is supported by the computation (B1, B3). Whether HPS in fact state a range is unverifiable here.
TOLERANCE ADDED BY THE TREE: MATCH_TOL = 5 % on both a and b (hpscentre.py:263) is the tree's own criterion ('the old control's own 5 %'), not HPS's; HPS give no uncertainty on a, b (as recorded).

NON-CONVERGENCE CLAIM (tree, hpscentre.py:171-172 'a has not converged to a constant in either system: it keeps rising with the window'): AGREES with the computation up to 1e5 K (local slope rises monotonically in both readings, B2), with the nuance that the increments shrink (printed: 0.609 -> 0.038 per unit ln l; conserved: 1.662 -> 0.308), so 'keeps rising' within the range is not a showing that no limit exists; the extrapolated limit depends on the model assumed (printed 5.64 under a power-law tail, 6.75 under a 1/ln l tail), so the limit is not determined by these data. Not a drift in the tree's wording, which claims only non-convergence in range.

ASYMPTOTIC FLATNESS PHRASING: the WebSearch abstract snippet says 'two asymptotically spatially flat regions'; Hochberg-Visser gr-qc/9802046 p.3 (Hochberg being an HPS author) says 'no asymptotically flat spatial regions'; the tree quotes HPS 'the metric as a whole is not asymptotically flat' (hpscentre.py:99-100). The far-zone law makes g_tt unbounded, so the full metric is not asymptotically flat on either reading; the 'spatially flat' vs 'no flat spatial regions' wording difference is recorded as a discrepancy between an abstract snippet and a later co-author paper, not adjudicated.

lacked_data: This result is a numerical fit to HPS's own integration; no measured physical constant enters (K is a pure number times l_P; ln f(0) is a boundary choice). So M's hypothesis cannot act through a moved datum. What HPS lacked in 1997 was (i) an independent second printing of the source term: Popov 2003 disagrees at three places, and the tree's conservation test singles out 116 at M1 where HPS print 16 (hpscentre.py:157-163); (ii) Popov's result that the AHS approximation is established under asymptotic flatness, which HPS's far zone lacks. Evidence either way on whether having it changes the conclusion: the conserved system's fits in windows starting at >= 2000 K are a = 6.7-8.9, b = 36-57, far from (5.3, 25.5) -- so the NUMBERS change if HPS integrated the printed system and the conserved one is right; but the printed-M1 system reproduces (5.3, 25.5) in 125/231 windows and the conserved one in 5/231 (small windows near 500-2900 K), and the tree's rule refuses an attribution because no window has exactly one matching system in every window (reproduced: NOT DETERMINED). The qualitative conclusion -- a logarithmically growing, non-flat far zone -- is shared by both readings. Unknown here: HPS's window and unit of l (source not read this run). Nothing presumed: the counts are reported, not converted into an attribution.
grade_evidence: The source could not be read this run (alphaXiv quota exceeded; every arXiv route and mirror EGRESS_BLOCKED), so the published statement, the unit of l, F = f and whether a fitting range is stated cannot be checked against HPS -- by the docket's rule that is OPEN, not STANDS. What WAS checked, and does not by itself move the grade: (1) the tree's use is fixture-only and already carries the window caveat (hpscentre.py:169-176, 241-245); (2) the re-run of the tree's integrations to 1e5 K reproduces its sweep and its NOT DETERMINED attribution exactly; (3) (5.3, 25.5) IS reproducible as a window fit in K units by the printed-M1 reading (125/231 windows, e.g. [2000,1e4] K -> (5.300, 25.049)) and marginally by the conserved reading (5/231), so the printed numbers are not refuted -- nothing here is WRONG; (4) the fitted coefficients depend on the window and the local slope has not reached a constant by 8e4 K in either reading, with an extrapolated limit that depends on the tail model assumed; so IF HPS present (5.3, 25.5) as an asymptotic constant rather than a fit over a range, the result would be NARROWED to a window fit -- conditional on a reading not possible here; (5) b depends on the unit of l (sympy): 25.5 in K units vs 51.48 if l were in l_P.
what_would_change_the_grade: Reading HPS p.8 at source (alphaXiv quota reset, or any reachable copy of gr-qc/9701064 / PRL 78 2050): (a) if HPS print a = 5.3, b = 25.5 in K units as a fit over a stated range that one reading reproduces there -> STANDS (as a window fit); (b) if HPS present them as the asymptotic far-zone law with no range -> NARROWED (the computation shows window dependence and no converged slope to 1e5 K in either reading of the system); (c) if HPS's l is in l_P or F is not the tree's f -> the fixture is mis-read (a discrepancy in the tree's reading, not a refutation of HPS), and the sweep would need re-running against the corrected target; (d) a determination of which system HPS integrated would make the numbers DATA-DEPENDENT on the source-term reading. An integration beyond 1e5 K showing a_loc levelling or growing without bound would settle convergence.
